description: Run Findings page — displays AI-detected issues and findings from a workflow run, organized by category with severity levels, filtering, auto-fix capabilities, and actionable recommendations.

groups.name: Findings Overview and Summary
groups.description: When users navigate to the Findings page, they need an immediate understanding of the overall issue landscape. The page header presents aggregate statistics — total findings count, actionable items, items needing user input, resolved items, and informational entries. This summary enables the user to quickly prioritize their attention: if there are critical actionable findings they need to address first, or if everything has been resolved. The report title and execution status round out the context.

assertions.description: The user can see aggregate statistics showing the total number of findings, how many are actionable, how many need user input, and how many have been resolved, enabling quick triage of the issue landscape

The user can see the execution report title and current status (running, completed, failed, etc.), providing context about which run these findings belong to and whether more findings may still be arriving
The user can distinguish between findings of different severity levels (critical, high, medium, low, info), allowing them to focus on the most impactful issues first

groups.name: Filtering and Navigation
groups.description: With potentially dozens of findings across multiple categories, users need robust filtering to focus on what matters. The page provides three independent filter dimensions — mode (all, actionable, needs input, resolved), severity (critical through info), and category (code bug, security, test issue, etc.). Users can combine these filters and clear them all at once. This filtering capability is essential for large reports where scanning every finding linearly would be impractical.

assertions.description: The user can filter findings by mode (all findings, actionable only, needs input, or resolved), reducing the visible set to only the findings that match their current workflow goal
The user can filter findings by severity level, allowing them to focus exclusively on critical or high-severity issues when time is limited
The user can filter findings by category (code bugs, security issues, test issues, documentation, etc.), allowing them to work through findings systematically by domain
The user can clear all active filters at once to return to the full unfiltered view, and can see a badge indicating how many filters are currently active

groups.name: Actions and Auto-Fix
groups.description: Findings are not just informational — they are actionable. Users can analyze individual findings, dismiss irrelevant ones, provide input when requested, and resolve issues. The auto-fix feature is a key differentiator: users can toggle automatic fixing of eligible issues (code bugs, security, tests, documentation) and trigger a bulk fix operation that sends all auto-fixable findings to AI for resolution. This transforms the findings page from a passive report into an active issue resolution workflow.

assertions.description: The user can toggle an auto-fix setting that enables or disables AI-driven automatic fixing of eligible findings, giving them control over whether the system proactively resolves issues
When auto-fixable findings exist, the user can trigger a bulk fix operation that sends all eligible findings to AI for resolution in a single action, dramatically reducing manual effort
The user can clear all findings from the report when they want to start fresh, such as after resolving all issues or before a new analysis run

groups.name: Categorized Findings Display
groups.description: Findings are organized into category sections (code bugs, security issues, test issues, documentation, performance, etc.), each with its own header, icon, and collapsible list of individual findings. This organization helps users work through issues domain by domain rather than facing an undifferentiated list. Each finding within a category shows its title, severity, description, and available actions (analyze, resolve, dismiss, provide input).

assertions.description: Findings are visually grouped into category sections, each with a distinct header showing the category name and finding count, so the user can see at a glance which areas have the most issues
Each individual finding displays its title, severity level, and description, giving the user enough information to understand the issue and decide whether to act on it
When no findings have been detected, the user sees a helpful empty state message encouraging them to run an AI analysis, rather than showing a confusing blank page

states.name: No Run Selected
states.description: The RunSelectionContext is present but no run has been chosen. The page shows an Activity icon and guidance text prompting the user to select a run from the Run Dashboard.

elements.textContains: Select a run from the Run Dashboard

transitions.name: User selects a run that has no findings
User selects a run that has findings

states.name: Empty — No Findings Yet
states.description: No findings have been detected. The page shows a FileText icon, 'No Findings Yet' heading, and a message encouraging the user to run an AI analysis.

transitions.name: Findings arrive from a live analysis or report load

states.name: Findings Displayed — Categories and Actions Visible
states.description: Findings are loaded and displayed. The header shows the report title, status badge, summary statistics (Total, Actionable, Needs Input, Resolved, Info), filter dropdowns (mode, severity, category), Auto-Fix toggle, and action buttons. Below, findings are grouped by category sections.

transitions.name: User selects a mode, severity, or category filter
User clicks Fix All to bulk-fix auto-fixable findings
User clicks Clear to remove all findings

states.name: Filters Active — Filtered Findings View
states.description: One or more filters are applied (mode, severity, or category). The active filter count badge and Clear button are visible. Category sections show filtered subsets with 'N of M' counts.

transitions.name: User clicks Fix All while filters are active
User clears all findings while filters are active

states.name: Auto-Fix Enabled
states.description: The Auto-Fix toggle is active. The toggle button shows a blue highlighted state indicating AI will automatically fix eligible issues. The rest of the findings display remains visible.

transitions.name: User clicks Fix All while auto-fix is enabled

states.name: Fixing In Progress — Bulk Fix Running
states.description: The Fix All bulk operation is running. The Fix All button shows a spinner and 'Fixing...' text. The button is disabled to prevent duplicate submissions. Findings remain visible underneath.

transitions.name: Bulk fix completes successfully or with errors
